title: fix(kernel): machining-mesh parity for the solidcore STEP path
body:
## What changed

This PR is part B0 of #917. It prepares the kernel and the geometry crate for the solidcore STEP path. It does not switch the import.

- **Coordinate snap** (`crates/kernel/src/mesh_weld.rs`). Each coordinate snaps to a grid of 1e-3 mm when it is within 1e-9 mm of a grid point. The snap runs before the exact-bit weld. It gives +0.0, not -0.0. A triangle that the snap collapses is dropped. `sides()` refuses a mesh that the drop opened.
- **Turn an inward solid outward** (`machining_mesh.rs`). A watertight mesh with a negative volume gets its winding reversed. The mesh keeps a note: "the solid's faces all pointed inward (volume -X mm^3); the mesh is turned outward".
- **Refuse a breaking spline by name** (`crates/kernel/src/step_curve_guard.rs`). A pre-scan of the STEP exchange refuses an edge or swept spline that breaks the subdivision. The message names "edge" or "swept" and "subdivision".
- **Adaptive refinement with a cap** (`mesh_deviation.rs`). `measure_within` refines to depth 12, with a budget of 1<<21 samples. The bound `dmax + longest 3D side` is a rigorous upper bound (the distance to a set is 1-Lipschitz, and a mesh triangle is flat). `measure` keeps depth 3. The analytic distance moved to `mesh_distance.rs` to keep the file under 400 lines.
- **Solid ranges in the mesh** (`crates/geometry`). `Mesh.solids` holds one facet range for each solid. An empty list means one soup. `Mesh::from_solids` validates the ranges. `slice::slice_of` slices the full mesh first. On a non-manifold result with two or more ranges, it slices each range and unites the results. An inward range keeps the refusal. A range out of bounds gives `SliceError::Invalid`.
- Eight app tests use `Mesh::from_facets` instead of a struct literal, because `Mesh` has a new field.

The decision file is `docs/decisions/917-kernel-parity.md`.

## Changed pins

| Test | Old | New | Cause |
|---|---|---|---|
| `machining_mesh` Solidcraft at 0.005 | replan: yes | replan: no (largest 0.0049999913) | the adaptive bound proves the first plan |
| `machining_mesh` Solidcraft at 0.1 | `largest() > 0.1`, replan: yes | `parametric > 0.1 && largest() <= 0.1`, replan: no (largest 0.0999999405) | the same |
| fillet_corner at 0.005 | refused | passes (largest 0.0049998025) | the same |

All other asserts stay. No tracked fixture replans now (checked: bspline_dome, spline_revolved, bar_cross_holes, fig8, twisted_flank, sample_ap214, Milling-test, modular_clamp_unit, Solidcraft from 0.002 to 0.2).

## Deviation

The snap pins are in `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs`, not in `crates/geometry/tests`. `geometry::step` is not on main, and a geometry-to-kernel edge would be necessary. The decision file records this.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh_parity.rs` (5 tests). These include: the noise goes; a point 1e-6 off a grid point stays; a collapsed facet is dropped; an inward solid turns outward.
- `crates/kernel/tests/step_curve_guard.rs` (4 tests).
- `crates/geometry/tests/mesh_solids.rs` (5 tests).
- `crates/kernel/tests/machining_mesh.rs` (7 tests, with the changed pins above).

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=12): wall 46.8 min, 948 steps, 0 failed, clippy `-D warnings` ok.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main`: wall 64.6 min, 232 steps, 0 failed.

## Not exercised

- The app import still uses the old STEP path. The switch, the app part of the solid ranges and the import tests come in PR B (stacked on this PR).
- No GUI run.

Changelog: none (no user-visible change until PR B switches the import)

Refs #917

title: feat(motion): equal depth steps as an opt-in ladder parameter
body:
## What changed

- The default depth ladder does not change. It keeps the remainder in the last step. `top 20, bottom 2, stepdown 5` cuts `[15, 10, 5, 2]`.
- A new operation parameter, `equal_steps`, is in the `links.approach` object. The default is off.
- With `equal_steps` on, the ladder cuts the same number of levels in equal steps. The same example cuts `[15.5, 11, 6.5, 2]`.
- `camcraft_motion::machining2d::equal_stepdown` gives the stepdown of the equal ladder. The level law `cut_levels_under` walks it. There is still one level law.
- `cut_levels_for(top, &approach, bottom, stepdown)` reads the mode and the stock top from the approach. These ladders call it: 2D Pocket (rings, adaptive, HSM, trochoidal, avoid), 2D Adaptive rest, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular (and its vault rings), 3D Pocket (plain, shell, rest refine).
- With stock above Top Z (#2004), the level at Top Z stays. The steps below it are equal.
- The project file writes `equal_steps` only when it is on. Older files load without a change.
- The params digest takes one byte only when the mode is on. The stamp of each existing operation does not change.
- The pocket region law of the app (`operation::area::ladder_planes`) reads the same mode through `OpParams::ladder_stepdown`. The region is built at the planes that the generator cuts.
- The Lead in / Lead out tab has one new row, "Equal depth steps", in the Linking group.
- `docs/decisions/2012-equal-steps.md` records the decision.

The parameter is undoable through `EditOperationParams`. The MCP `edit_operation` patch reaches it as `params.links.approach.equal_steps`. No new command and no new MCP tool are necessary.

## Cause

Issue #2012 asks for a decision between a remainder last step and equal steps. The level law had only the remainder ladder. The project rule "CAM choices are parameters" asks for a parameter with a default.

## Scope limit

Face, Trace, Engrave and Trochoidal Slot have no `links` object. They cannot save the parameter and keep the remainder ladder. Issue #2832 adds the parameter to them. Turning has its own infeed laws and is not part of this change.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `the_default_ladder_keeps_the_remainder_and_equal_steps_is_opt_in`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_count_and_never_pass_the_stepdown`
- `equal_steps_keep_the_level_at_top_z_under_stock`
- `equal_steps_refuse_what_the_remainder_ladder_refuses`
- `a_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_trochoidal_adaptive_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_slot_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_bore_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_circular_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `a_3d_pocket_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs`:

- `edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`
- `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back`
- `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`
- `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode`
- `the_generated_contour_cuts_the_levels_of_its_mode`
- `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps`

Red before the change: yes. The motion pin did not compile on `upstream/main` 3970d3d03 (`Approach` has no field `equal_steps`; `cut_levels_for` and `equal_stepdown` do not exist).

Mutation results:

- Mutation 1: `ladder_stepdown` ignores the mode. Result: red. 10 of the 11 motion pins fail. The refusal pin stays green, which is correct.
- Mutation 2: the 12 caller files are the files of `upstream/main`, and the new law stays. Result: red. The 7 operation pins fail. The 4 law pins stay green.
- Mutation 3: the digest byte and the DTO write are removed. Result: red. `the_stamp_tells_the_two_ladders_apart`, `the_project_file_writes_equal_steps_only_when_on_and_reads_it_back` and `mcp_edit_operation_reaches_equal_steps` fail.
- After each mutation the code was restored and the pins were green again.

The first stamp pin did not fail in mutation 3. A default approach hashes no bytes, so each approach that is not the default already has a different stamp. The pin now also compares two approaches that are not the default.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` ran on `6ba261db2`: 162 steps, 161 green, 1 red.
- The red step was `ui suites: lib`. The test binary stopped with `signal: 11, SIGSEGV` after 3 s. No test reported a failure.
- The same step ran again alone (`--failed`) with no code change. It was green in 205 s.
- An intermittent SIGSEGV of a UI test binary on `main` is recorded in #2807. Its cause is not known. This run does not show whether this PR is related to it.
- After the gate, one assert line in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs` changed for clippy (head `13c4dffab`). The motion pins ran again and are green. The full quick gate did not run again on that head.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on the final head.

File length: `crates/motion/src/approach.rs` was 440 lines and is now 446. `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs` is now 402 lines.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.cnc"` is empty. The default ladder is the same.

## Not exercised

- No pin generates these ladders with the mode on: the pocket with keep-out areas (`pocket_avoid`), the 2D Adaptive rest ladder, the Circular vault rings, the 3D Pocket shell and rest-refine ladders, the rotary and multi-axis roughing. They call the same function as the pinned ladders.
- No pin generates a pocket on a part with the mode on. `the_region_law_reads_the_stepdown_of_the_ladder_mode` pins the stepdown that the region law reads, not the region.
- Code that reads `stepdown` as a bound is not changed (the 3-D shell floor below a plane, the first entry height of the contour). With equal steps it reads a bound a little larger than the real step. The decision file records this.
- The new UI row has no test of its own. No snapshot PNG is changed.
- The heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy`) were not run.
- Nothing was run on a machine or in the stock simulation.

## Overlaps

- #2678 (`needs-rework`, `conflicts`) changes `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs`. It replaces the same `cut_levels_under` calls with its own `floor_levels::cut_levels`. It also changes `levels.rs`, but in `run_level_walks`, which this PR does not change. This PR is not stacked on #2678, because #2678 does not merge with `main` now. Whichever merges second refreshes, and must keep the mode in the 3-D ladder.
- #2796 changes `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs`, in a different function. Whichever merges second refreshes.
- #2716 and #2714 change `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`. This PR does not change that file.

Build note: the shared sccache server on the build machine did not answer. The tests and gates ran with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=` and `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`.

Effort: high

Changelog: Depth ladder: new operation parameter "Equal depth steps" (off by default) cuts the same number of levels in equal steps; the default ladder keeps the remainder in the last step (#2012).

Fixes #2012

title: perf(sim): share unchanged cut bricks between playback keyframes
body:
## What changed

- The three cut layers of `SdfField` (`cuts`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`) hold each brick in an `Arc` (`CutLayer`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs`).
- A clone of the field copies the keys and the pointers only. It shares the bricks.
- A write goes through `layer_brick_mut` (`Arc::make_mut`). It copies a brick first when a clone still holds that brick.
- `claim_record` and `up_record` read the cell first. They take the writable brick only when the value changes. A move that changes no cell copies no brick.
- `KeyCost` has a new method, `key_bytes_after(prev)`. The keyframe store counts a keyframe by the bricks that the keyframe before it does not share, and by its map entries.
- `Keyframes::offer` and `Keyframes::held_bytes` use that count. The budget, the thinning and the stride law do not change.
- The public API of the sim crate only grows: `SdfField::cut_bytes_after` and `KeyCost::key_bytes_after` (with a default).

## Cause

A playback keyframe was a whole copy of the cut layers (#2181, PR #2192). Two keyframes one stride apart differ only in the bricks that the moves between them changed. The store paid for all bricks in each keyframe.

## Readings

Dense 100 mm face (`precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face`, release, 4268 moves, 68 keyframes, stride 64):

| | Keyframe bytes | Calculation time |
|---|---|---|
| `upstream/main` (old sim sources) | 444 940 288 (424 MiB) | 49.8 s |
| This PR | 65 181 664 (62 MiB) | 30 s to 32 s (three runs) |

The factor is 6.8. The test asserts a factor of 6 at least.
The machine had other builds in progress, so the times are not exact.

Staged 24 mm face at 0.5 mm cells (debug, 28 keyframes): 9 923 808 bytes held. Whole copies cost 45 301 760 bytes. The factor is 4.56. The test asserts a factor of 4 at least.

## Tests

Pins:

- `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` (`crates/app/tests/stock_play_precalc.rs`). It asserts the factor of 4, the equality of the running count and the audit, and the bit-identical replay at six positions.
- `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts the count on plain values, before and after a thinning.
- `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` (`crates/sim/tests/play_keys.rs`). It asserts that a clone is not written through, and that the cut over shared bricks is the plain cut, bit for bit.
- `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` (heavy lane, release). It now asserts the factor of 6 on the dense face.

Red before the fix: the first pin failed on unchanged code with `8454144 bytes held; whole copies cost 8454144`.

Mutations (each one red, then green after the restore):

- `offer` counts `value.key_bytes()` (the old line): `a_keyframe_costs_what_the_one_before_does_not_share` is red.
- `held_bytes` sums whole copies (the old line): the same test is red, `(5, 1, 40, 100)` against `(5, 1, 40, 40)`.
- `layer_brick_mut` writes through the shared pointer: `a_clone_shares_its_cut_bricks_and_a_write_copies_first` is red at "a shared brick is copied before the write".
- `claim_record` takes the writable slot before the read: `the_keyframes_share_the_bricks_that_no_move_changed` is red, `16358624 bytes held; whole copies cost 45301760`.
- All of `crates/sim/src` from `upstream/main`: `precalc_reading_on_the_dense_face` is red, `444940288 bytes held; whole copies cost 444940288`.

Unchanged and green: `the_precalculated_stock_is_the_live_cut_at_every_position`, `a_live_seek_after_a_cancel_keeps_the_byte_budget`, `the_worker_calculates_first_then_replays_and_the_post_gate_is_unchanged` (the replay is bit-identical, the budget holds, the post gate reads the same).

Gate on the final head: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green, 11 steps, 0 failed (sim lib, `play_keys`, `play_precalc`, `stock_carry_side_exact`, `stock_columns`, `stock_field_cost`, `stock_sdf`; app `stock_field_cost`, `stock_play_precalc`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Heavy lanes that ran (release, `--ignored`): app `stock_play_precalc` and app `stock_field_cost`. The two are green.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` plans 217 steps for this diff. Only the two heavy binaries above ran. The other heavy lanes did not run. Run them before this PR is flagged ready.
- The `camcraft-ui` crate was not built. This PR changes no item that the UI crate can see, other than the two additions.
- The gate and the tests ran without sccache and with a target directory outside the worktree. The sccache daemon on this machine executed no compile, and a stuck `cargo check` of the editor tooling held the build lock of the worktree.
- `CostLedger` (the cut region, the full-brick ledger, the dirty set) is still copied whole by each keyframe. The store does not count it, as before.
- The time of one cell write was not measured alone. The dense face calculation as a whole is faster.

## Overlaps

PR #2714 changes other files in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/` and `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`. It changes none of the files of this PR.

Decision: `docs/decisions/2194-share-keyframe-bricks.md`.

Effort: max

Changelog: Simulation playback: keyframes share the stock bricks that no move changed, so the calculation before playback uses much less memory (the dense 100 mm face: 62 MiB, before 424 MiB) and keeps a shorter stride on large programs.

Fixes #2194

title: fix(xtask): derive the gate job budget from available CPUs
body:
## What changed

The default gate budget uses `std::thread::available_parallelism()`.
The default has a floor of 2 and a cap of 64.
CPU detection failure uses 2 jobs.
`CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS` still accepts any positive whole number.
The plan prints the budget and its source, including in `--dry-run`.
Batch and release already share the budget over dynamic lanes.
Builds, isolated tests, UI steps and clippy keep the full budget.
The lane fixtures use an explicit budget of six.
AGENTS.md and the gate skill describe the new default.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/2814-core-budget.md`.

Process change: yes

## Cause

`budget::DEFAULT` fixed the automatic budget at six.
Larger machines left available CPUs idle unless a runner owner set the override.

## Tests

All pins are in `xtask/src/budget_tests.rs`:

- `the_default_budget_uses_the_available_cpus`
- `the_override_reports_its_source`
- `the_default_budget_has_a_floor_and_cap_with_mock_cpus`
- `an_explicit_budget_is_not_limited_by_the_cpu_floor_or_cap`
- `an_invalid_budget_uses_the_cpu_default_and_names_the_bad_input`

The first two pins failed on unchanged code.
The host default was six instead of 32, and the override had no source note.
The deterministic pins cover missing CPUs, zero, one, the bounds, large counts, empty values and invalid overrides.

Mutation checks:

- Restore `upstream/main:xtask/src/budget.rs` with compatible initial pins: red; restore the fix: green.
- Change the CPU fallback to six: red; restore: green.
- Remove the floor: red; restore: green.
- Remove the cap: red; restore: green.
- Clamp explicit overrides: red; restore: green.

Each mutation failed a runtime assertion.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 196 unit tests and 22 integration tests.
The gate took 317 seconds, including a cold application build for a catalog test.
`cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.

`cargo xtask gate batch --dry-run` passed without `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS`.
It reported 32 available CPUs, 32 jobs and at most 16 lanes.
The queue used 16 lanes with two jobs each.
Alone steps received 32 jobs.

The gate used base `380c29b3c`.
Upstream advanced with #2809 during verification.
That change does not touch these files.
The branch has no refresh merge.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty.

## Not exercised

A full batch or release gate did not run.
Windows and macOS did not run.
The optional memory guard is omitted.
CPU detection failure is covered through injected values.
The final documentation was added after the green gate, as the requested procedure specifies.

## Overlaps

- #2825 touches `xtask/src/exec.rs`: same file, different function; whichever merges second refreshes.
  This PR changes `Run::plan`.
  #2825 changes `Run::new`, `Run::step` and `Run::execute`.
- #2787 touches `xtask/src/exec.rs` and AGENTS.md: same file, different function or section; whichever merges second refreshes.
  It changes `Run::summary` and the light-lane rules.
  This PR adds the budget rule near the compile-cache rule.

Effort: medium

Changelog: The gate uses the available CPU count for its default job budget, with a floor of 2 and a cap of 64.

Fixes #2814

title: fix(sinker): judge body electrodes against cavity outlines
body:
Stacked on #2714 (merge #2714 first)

## What changed

This fix changes 23 files relative to parent `b95c27b2e`.
It adds `cavity_outline` to Sinker Burn parameters.
The points use coordinates relative to the burn point.
The project file, operation digest and MCP tools carry the outline.
An empty outline keeps the previous extent law.

The size law compares the electrode with inward cavity wall offsets.
It permits the derived diamond finish electrode.
It still refuses an oversized electrode by name.
It also refuses malformed outlines, contradictory dimensions and an incomplete finish.
Command creation checks the outline and its stated dimensions.
Generation repeats the bounds checks.
The existing scalar law keeps the floor and condition checks.

The MCP schema declares an optional array with a `null` default.
The electrode reply supplies an array for a body and `null` for a rectangle.
A `null` params patch clears the outline.
The independent stock verdict still checks the actual burn.

## Cause

The previous law judged X and Y extents.
An inward offset moves a sharp diamond corner farther than the condition's undersize.
The correct finish electrode then failed the extent check.
The original pin reported a burned X extent of `19.962` for a `20.000` cavity.

## Tests

The original pin failed before the production change:

- `a_diamond_cavity_finish_is_generated_and_judged_clean`

The MCP pin covers schema discovery, translated outlines, generation, null clearing and early refusals:

- `mcp_exposes_the_cavity_outline_and_burns_a_diamond_finish`

Final targeted runs passed 11 app tests and 10 motion tests.

The parent base predates the following upstream additions.
They appear absent in this comparison.
Commit `b94e2692f` added the first file.
Commit `f1485e26e` added the remaining eight files.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/pocket3d_trochoidal_pocket.cl`

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

title: fix(drilling): Back bore (G89) carries the dwell and feeds out at the plunge feed
body:
## What changed

- The drill generator now writes the user's dwell into the `Cycle` record of a Back bore (G89) hole.
- The Back bore chain now feeds out at the plunge feed. This is the same feed as the feed in.
- No post changed. No golden file changed.

Files:

- `crates/motion/src/drilling/cycle.rs`: the two changes above.
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests_backbore.rs`: the two pinning tests (new file).
- `crates/motion/src/drilling/mod.rs`: registers the test module.
- `docs/decisions/1480-backbore-dwell.md`: the decision entry.

## Cause

`drill()` set the dwell of a Back bore hole to 0. The dwell of the user did not reach the cycle record, the simulation or a post.

`drill()` also fed out at the cutting feed. A canned G89 has one F word, and the post takes it from the first cutting move of the hole, which is the plunge. The control fed out at the plunge feed, but the CL chain said the cutting feed. The verifier and the simulation read a different motion than the machine ran.

## Dwell unit for each post

The posts already read the dwell in seconds and write their own P unit. This PR does not change them. These tests on `main` pin the words:

- Fanuc, Mazak, Doosan: `G89 ... P500` (whole milliseconds). `crates/post/tests/dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs`.
- grblHAL, Tormach, LinuxCNC: `G89 ... P0.5` (seconds). The same file.
- Haas: `G89 ... P500`. `crates/post/tests/haas_dwell_cycles.rs`.
- Mach4: `G89 ... P0.25` (seconds). `crates/post/tests/mach4_post.rs`.
- Heidenhain: an explicit chain with one `FUNCTION DWELL TIME` block. `crates/post/tests/heidenhain_cycles.rs`.
- The lathe posts and the posts with no canned cycle refuse the Back bore by name.

## Tests

Pins (`camcraft-motion`, lib):

- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_carries_the_dwell`
- `drilling::tests_backbore::back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`

Red on unchanged code:

- `back_bore_carries_the_dwell`: `G89 dwells at the bottom: the cycle record carries the user's 1.5 s, got 0`.
- `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed`: `left: Some(500.0) right: Some(100.0)`.

Mutations:

- The old feed-out feed (`p.feed`) put back: `back_bore_feeds_in_and_out_at_the_plunge_feed` is red. Restored: green.
- `CycleKind::BackBore` removed from the dwell list: `back_bore_carries_the_dwell` is red. Restored: green.

Gate on head `b86a07482`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 19 steps, 0 failed (motion lib, 3 motion suites, 13 app suites).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1`. The shared sccache server of the build machine did not answer, and each compiler call stopped there.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main...HEAD -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` is empty. No recorded program has a Back bore that the generator makes.

## Not exercised

- No heavy lane ran (`cargo xtask gate heavy`). Run it before this PR is flagged ready.
- No test posts a generated Back bore with a dwell from the operation to the G-code in one run. The generator pin and the post pins meet at the `Cycle` record.
- The Sinumerik post writes `P` in whole milliseconds on G89. No test pins that word, and its source comment verifies P for G82 and G83 only. This PR does not change that post. A follow-up issue can pin it or refuse it.
- The Heidenhain post writes the Back bore as an explicit chain. Its retract line now has the plunge feed for a generated Back bore. The existing Heidenhain test uses a recorded chain and did not change.
- The UI was not started.

## Behaviour that changes for a program with no dwell

A Back bore with no dwell posts the same canned block as before (G85 or G89, with the same F). Its `.cl` chain changes: the feed out is now the plunge feed. The simulation time of the retract changes with it.

## Overlaps

None. No open PR changes a file in `crates/motion/src/drilling/`.

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Pocket from the previous operations
body:
## What changed

The rest group of the 2D Pocket has a new mode, "previous operations".
In this mode the rest area is read from the stock that the earlier operations of the same setup leave.
The entered-tool mode of #1489 does not change, and it stays the default.

- `RestParams` has the field `source` (`RestSource::EnteredTool` or `RestSource::PreviousOperations`).
- `machining2d::rest_pocket_previous` plans the rest passes from a column grid.
  `rest_stock_from_columns` builds the `RestStock` of #2031 from that grid, one floor for each cut depth.
  `rest_plan_stock` makes the rest area from it.
- The grid is the one that `rest::prior_state` builds for the 3D Pocket: the setup stock, cut by the cached paths of the earlier operations, each with its tool shape.
- The reading is conservative:
  - A column stands at a cut depth when its top is above that depth. A floor allowance is material.
  - The standing columns grow by one cell diagonal.
  - A column that cannot be read stands. The pocket outside the grid stands.
  - The rest area is the union over all cut depths. A roughing pass that stops above the floor leaves the whole pocket.
- The two modes never use the planner of the other mode. Each planner refuses the other mode by name.
- The mode rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest.source` and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter.
  A file without the key reads as the entered tool.
- The Pocket page has the row "Rest stock from". The previous tool rows hide in the new mode.

Generation refuses by name when the stock cannot be established:

- an earlier operation of the setup has no toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup has a stale toolpath;
- an earlier operation of the setup is suppressed and has a cut on record;
- the Pocket is tilted (also refused at the edit).

When no earlier operation cut, the stock is known. The whole pocket is cut and a note says it.

## Cause

The rest generator trusted the entered previous tool.
It could not see the depth that the earlier operation reached (#1490, item 3).

## Tests

Pins, all new:

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_tests.rs` (lib): `each_reading_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `a_floor_cut_at_the_cut_depth_does_not_stand_and_one_above_it_does`, `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_previous.rs`: 6 tests. They compare the rest area with an independent simulation of the earlier operations: a flat tool, a wall allowance, a bull-nose tool, mixed tools with a partial depth and disconnected cuts, an island. The rest path cuts each column that was left and cuts no wall.
- `crates/app/tests/rest_previous_ops.rs`: 7 tests. The real job against an independent simulation; the shallow roughing pass; the four refusals; stale after a changed tool, depth and order; `RegenerateAll`; undo and redo; the project file; MCP with save and reopen.
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` now also covers the mode.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/rest_source_tests.rs`: 2 tests for the new row.

Red before the change: the pins use the new API and do not compile on `upstream/main`. Thus the mutation results below are the proof for each guard.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant | Restored |
|---|---|---|---|
| every cut depth is read (`Guards::depth`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| an unreadable column stands (`Guards::unknown`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| the pocket outside the grid stands (`Guards::outside`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| one cell of growth (`Guards::cell`) | `each_reading_guard_...` | red | green |
| `rest_plan` refuses the new mode | `the_two_rest_modes_never_use_each_others_planner` | red | green |
| `rest_pocket_previous` refuses the entered mode | same | red | green |
| `validate` does not read the previous tool in the new mode | same | red | green |
| job: tilted plane refused | `a_tilted_plane_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit_and_at_generation` | red | green |
| door: tilted plane refused at the edit | same | red | green |
| job: `previous_ops_refusal` is called | `a_stock_that_cannot_be_established_is_refused_by_name` | red | green |
| earlier operation suppressed | same | red | green |
| earlier operation stale | same | red | green |
| earlier operation never generated | same | red | green |
| the Pocket arm routes the mode | `the_rest_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left` | red | green |
| stamp byte 0xD8 | `the_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red | green |

The first four guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off. The other eleven were removed by hand.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head merged with `upstream/main` c4ac3ce6d: green, 357 steps, 0 failed (29.2 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved

None. `git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl" "*.png"` is empty.

## Not exercised

- A setup whose stock is carried from an earlier setup (#318). The code path is `rest::prior_state`, which the 3D Pocket uses. No test here crosses a setup boundary. The check for stale operations reads the same setup only.
- A WCS yaw. The existing `wcs_yaw::enter` turns the grid. No test here has a yaw.
- The field stock engine (#586, #637). The reader is `Columns`, which reads the two engines. The tests use the column grid.
- Zigzag and Offset rings in the new mode. They use the passes of the entered-tool mode, which has its own tests. The new tests use Waterline.
- The pixel snapshots (release lane). The new row moves the rows of a Pocket page that has rest machining on.
- The app was not started by hand. The UI tests ran the page in the test harness.

## Known limits (recorded in `docs/decisions/2033-rest-previous-ops.md`)

- One rest area for all levels. An upper level can cut air where only a lower level has material.
- The strict reading keeps a band of about 1.5 cells along each wall that an earlier tool rode. The rest pass follows those walls.
- The Adaptive strategy stays refused. The Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket is retired, so `rest_adaptive` has no door from this operation.
- The MCP skill text (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`) does not describe the new `source` key. The session could not write that file. That edit is owed.
- The guide pages on the site do not describe the new mode.

- #2678 changes `generate.rs`, `job.rs` and `machining2d/mod.rs`. Its hunks are not in the rest branch of the Pocket arm. The PR that merges second refreshes.

## What changed

- A new undoable command, `VouchModelFidelity { model, by }`, clears the "fidelity unknown" mark of one model. It also clears the mark of each stock that is copied straight from that model.
- The command is one labelled undo step. The label names the person who vouched. Undo puts each mark back.
- The command refuses by name:
  - a model with a recorded coarse chord (#864);
  - an incomplete model (#1610);
  - a model that is not marked;
  - a name that is not a model;
  - an empty name of the person who vouches.
- A new component, `FidelityVouched { by, rev }`, records who vouched. The record is valid only while the model has the same geometry revision and no fidelity flag.
- The project file keeps the record in the optional key `fidelity_vouched` of the model row. There is no project version step.
- The MCP tool `vouch_model_fidelity { model, by }` runs the same command. `get_job` shows `models[].fidelity_vouched`. A script uses the tool through `cam.call`.

Since project v59, each mesh of an older project without a recorded chord loads as "fidelity unknown" (#1056). The gate refuses its operations until a re-import. A model whose source file is gone, or whose mesh is exact, had no other path to a post.

title: fix(motion): keep circular ramp transitions at depth
body:
## What changed

Circular Ramp entries stay at depth between eligible levels of one ring.
The generator uses the existing certified KeepDown link.
Each new ring still enters from clearance.
The final retract stays in place.

The first ramp starts at most 0.1 mm above the remaining material.
A smaller configured gap stays in use.
The remaining material height keeps the rapid above stock over Top Z.
Explicit Retract links and other transition types keep their selected lift planes.
Ramp-to-depth entries keep their lift behavior.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/1807-circular-stay-down.md`.

title: feat(2d): place typed text as single-line engraving strokes (InsertText, MCP insert_text)
body:
First slice of #2679. This PR does not close the issue.

## What changed

- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/` is new. It holds our own single-line engraving font and the layout of a typed string.
  - `glyphs.rs` is the glyph table: capital letters, digits, the space and `- _ . : / # + = ( )`. Each glyph is straight strokes on a 4 x 6 grid.
  - `mod.rs` has `strokes()` (polylines in mm) and `sketch()` (a `SketchData` on the layer `text`).
- `crates/app/src/commands/insert_text.rs` is new. `InsertText` is an undoable command. It places the typed text as a `Sketch` on the top face of the stock of a setup, at X, Y and an angle.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/sketch_tools.rs` has the new MCP tool `insert_text`. It calls `InsertText`.
- `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` lists the tool.
- `docs/decisions/2679-engrave-typed-text.md` records the decisions.

The text profile is the same entity as a DXF profile. `move_dxf_profile`, `DeleteEntity`, `get_job` and the project file work on it with no change. The project file format does not change.

## Cause

There was no way to make 2D geometry from typed text. A user had to draw the letters in a CAD program and import a DXF file.

Two facts of `main` set the scope of this slice:

1. The issue says to use a font from `assets/ui/fonts/`. The repository holds no font file. The outlines of the `egui` default fonts need a font parser as a new dependency. A new dependency waits for the maintainer. This PR uses our own stroke font, drawn from scratch. A single-line stroke is also the correct input for the centreline Engrave generator: it gives a solid mark, not a hollow letter.
2. On `main`, an operation on a profile refuses generation by name ("a toolpath from the chains of a DXF profile is not generated yet"). #1869 adds Engrave and Trace on sketch chains, and #1869 depends on #1864 (PR #2716). The toolpath, the verify and the golden CL of #2679 need #1869.

## Refusals by name

- An empty text.
- A character with no glyph. A lower-case letter is refused. It is not changed to a capital, because a silent change puts a wrong mark on a part.
- A cap height outside 0.5 mm to 1000 mm. A letter spacing outside 0 mm to 1000 mm. More than 256 characters.
- A placement that is not finite or is more than 1e6 mm from the stock origin.
- A setup that does not exist. A setup with no stock. A name in use or a reserved name.
- `stroke_text::sketch` fails if a stroke does not chain clean. A text profile cannot hold a rejected chain.

## Tests

Pins (red before the change: the test files did not compile, `unresolved import camcraft_geometry::stroke_text`):

- `crates/geometry/tests/stroke_text.rs`
  - `a_known_string_gives_its_golden_strokes` (golden strokes of `SN-0471`)
  - `each_glyph_chains_with_no_rejection_at_the_extreme_heights`
  - `the_whole_character_set_in_one_string_chains_clean`
  - `the_sketch_is_in_millimetres_on_one_layer_with_the_cap_height_stated`
  - `height_scales_and_letter_spacing_moves_only_the_later_glyphs`
  - `bad_input_is_refused_by_name`
- `crates/geometry/src/stroke_text/mod.rs`: `the_character_set_is_the_glyph_table`, `each_glyph_stays_in_its_box`
- `crates/app/tests/insert_text.rs`
  - `typed_text_lands_as_a_placed_profile_and_undoes`
  - `bad_text_and_bad_places_are_refused_by_name_and_nothing_lands`
  - `a_text_profile_saves_and_loads_with_its_strokes_and_place`
  - `the_mcp_tool_places_text_reports_it_and_takes_an_engrave_operation`

Mutations (each guard removed, the pin run, the guard restored):

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `Y` drawn with three stroke ends at one corner | red: `each_glyph_chains_...`, `the_whole_character_set_...` ("3 curve ends meet ... a chain cannot branch") |
| Height check removed in `strokes()` | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Letter spacing check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Length check removed | red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` |
| Empty-text check removed in `strokes()` | green at first, so the pin was made stricter; then red: `bad_input_is_refused_by_name` (`Ok([])` in place of `Err(Empty)`) |
| No-stock check removed in `InsertText` | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...`, `the_mcp_tool_places_text_...` |
| Finite-placement check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Placement range check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |
| Reserved-name check removed | red: `bad_text_and_bad_places_...` |

With all guards restored, all pins are green.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green. The change touches the shared crate `camcraft-geometry`, so the quick tier ran as the batch tier.

- Run 1: build, geometry (with `stroke_text`), kernel, cl, tools, post and sim suites: 227 steps ok. The worker tool stopped this run at its time limit in step 228 (`motion suites: lib`). It was not a test failure.
- Run 2 (`--only "motion suites" --only "app suites" --only "ui suites" --only "clippy"`): 709 steps, 0 failed, 53.4 min. `clippy -D warnings` with `--all-targets` on each crate is ok.
- After the gate, one doc comment in `crates/app/src/schema.rs` changed (it names `InsertText` as a writer of `Sketch`). Then `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the suites `insert_text`, `mcp_dxf` and `sketch_project` ran again: all ok.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and no `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. With sccache, each compile stopped with no progress on this machine.

None. No `.nc` file and no `.cl` file changes. No snapshot PNG changes.

## Not exercised

- No toolpath, no verify and no posted G-code from a text profile. Generation from profile chains is refused by name on `main` until #1869.
- No UI. There is no dialog and no viewport placement in this PR. The command and the MCP tool are the only doors.
- No script verb `cam.insertText`.
- Placement on a model face. A `Sketch` lies on the top face of the stock only.
- The heavy lanes. This PR adds no generator and changes no existing geometry function.

## Open work for #2679 after this PR

- The Engrave toolpath, verify, post and golden CL on a text profile (needs #1869).
- The UI: type the text, pick the spot, set the height.
- The text as an editable parameter (needs a schema field and a project version step).
- Lower-case glyphs and an outline font source, if the maintainer wants them.
- The refusals for a text profile say "DXF profile". The wording is shared with DXF profiles and with PR #2716.
- The row for `insert_text` in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The worker session could not edit that file (the permission system blocked the edit). The tool description and `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` have the same facts.

## Overlaps

- PR #2773 changes `ImportDxf::build` and `sketch::face_frame` / `sketch::stock_face`. This PR calls `sketch::face_frame` and does not change it. The files are different. After #2773 merges, `InsertText` can use `stock_face` for the named refusal of a stock with no flat top.
- PR #2716 changes `sketch_model.rs` and the operation code. This PR does not touch those files.
- PR #2678 adds lines to `crates/app/src/commands/mod.rs` and `site/content/guide/automate/mcp.md` (different lines; the PR that merges second refreshes).
- The branch starts at `e048b103c`, and the gate ran on that base. `main` moved to `c4ac3ce6d` during the gate (#2149 and others merged). `git merge-tree upstream/main HEAD` gives no conflict.

Effort: high

Refs #2679

## What changed

Posts can declare `toolChangeMacros = { before: "M100\nM101", after: "M102" }`.
Both fields are optional strings.
The engine emits the literal NC lines around the complete `onToolChange` hook.

Macro lines belong to the TOOL record in the preview trace and line map.
Empty macros preserve the existing output.

## Cause

The engine had no generic macro configuration around tool-change hooks.
Repeated TOOL records can occur without a physical tool change.
The wrapper tracks tool numbers to avoid repeating macros for an unchanged tool.

title: fix(kernel): make STEP pcurves on the solidcore kernel
body:
## What changed

This PR moves the solidcore pin and lets the solidcore kernel make the pcurves (2D trims) that a STEP file does not give. It is part A of #917. Part B (the importer switch) stacks on this PR.

- `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`: the solidcore pin moves from `55d0e76` to `2016386442dfee3b2a0c3a1bfdd4017c5254dac8` (the fork sync of 2026-11-19).
- `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs` (new, with `solidcore_trims/checks.rs`): `KernelTrims` implements the solidcore `Trims` seam. It makes each pcurve on the kernel. It measures the gap of each bare edge to its face, and refuses an edge that is more than `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM` = 0.01 mm off its face. The tolerance in the file does not change this cap.
  - The lift check holds a made pcurve to the edge's tolerance, but never to more than `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM`.
  - A face, edge or vertex tolerance that is not a finite number of zero or more is refused by name. A lift sample whose distance is not finite is refused by name. (`f64::max` drops a NaN, so each value is checked before it is used.)
- `docs/decisions/917-kernel-pcurves.md`: the decisions and the dropped options.

## Readings

| Fixture | Edge gap | Verdict on this branch |
|---|---|---|
| fig8 | 3.5e-12 mm | agree |
| fillet_corner | 8.2e-13 mm | watertight, within tolerance (truck mesh is open: 121 open edges) |
| bar_cross_holes | 1.19e-6 mm | watertight, within tolerance (truck mesh is open: 1090 open edges) |
| bspline_discontinuous | 0.25 mm | refused (see below) |
| twisted_flank (new, our own) | does not reach KernelTrims: the reader makes its pcurves | read |
| Milling-test, Milling-test-inch | - | agree (was "disagree: bounding box"; the port's box at 2016386 stops at the flat, Refs #939) |

**Which fixtures reach KernelTrims.** A probe (removed before the commit) showed that fillet_corner, bar_cross_holes and fig8 reach it, and bspline_discontinuous reaches it until the gap cap refuses it. The two twisted_flank files do not reach it. `step_closed_form.rs` pins the KernelTrims route. The gate map line of `step_twisted_flank.rs` now says this.

**The lift tolerance.** The lift check uses `min(held, MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM)`. The held tolerances on the fixtures are 1e-6 mm (fillet_corner) and 2e-5 mm (bar_cross_holes), under the cap, so no verdict changes. The largest lift gaps are at most 2.9e-7 mm (fillet_corner) and 1.2e-5 mm (bar_cross_holes). All volumes stay the same and the two refused fixtures stay refused. The decision file records the readings.

**bspline_discontinuous stays refused.** The rule is the cap `MAX_EDGE_GAP_MM` = 0.01 mm in `cover_gaps` (`crates/kernel/src/solidcore_trims.rs`). The refusal text is: `#16 at read: pcurves failed on 1 of 6 faces; first: face #53: kernel pcurves: edge 0 lies 0.2500 mm off the face's surface, over the cap of 0.01 mm`. The pin is `step_twisted_flank::an_edge_a_quarter_millimetre_off_its_face_is_refused_by_name`, and the `step_agreement` row is "both refuse".

**Independent volume tests** (`crates/kernel/tests/step_closed_form.rs`). Each test compares the kernel's exact volume with a closed form that comes from the fixture's own dimensions (rel 1e-5), and checks the box (1e-6) and solidcore's own closed mesh (rel 1e-3):
- `fillet_corner_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume`: closed form 26816.4939 mm3, reading 26816.49 mm3.
- `bar_cross_holes_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume`: closed form 78225.6805 mm3, reading 78225.68 mm3.
- `fillet_corner_in_inches_reads_at_its_closed_form_volume_in_mm`: the test changes the length unit of `fillet_corner.step` to the inch in memory. The volume is 25.4^3 times the closed form, in mm, and the box is +-381 mm.

## Port pins that the pin move changed (re-triage)

The cause of all three is the solidcore move `55d0e76` -> `2016386`. KernelTrims is not the cause: none of these tests reads STEP.

1. `blend`: the rim chamfer's default path now gives the cone (upstream WR-421, solidcore#420). The test `not_yet_rim_chamfer_default_path_stays_a_finding` asked for a promotion. It is now `rim_chamfer_default_path_matches_the_cone`. This test heals the result to a closed solid and measures it against the cone's closed form (volume and box).
2. `corrupt_input`: "box at NaN origin" changes from "Ok non-solid" to "Err". The refusal is the stricter verdict. The pin is now "Err", with a comment that names the rev. The other 14 rows do not change.
3. `import_corpus`: the writer now prints the zone tolerance as `1e-5`, not `0.0000100000000000`. The literal corpus edit changed nothing, so the zero, negative and NaN rows read the intact box. The reader does not accept a NaN tolerance: `read_smb` refuses a non-finite tolerance by name. The edit now finds the header line by its label. The corpus test asserts that each edit changes the file. The new test `non_finite_zone_tolerance_is_refused_by_name` asserts the refusal text for NaN, inf and -inf. All rows of `KNOWN_SMB_VERDICTS` keep their pins.

No test was deleted, ignored or loosened. ## What changed

- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` (`minus_standing`): the result "enclosed area minus standing part material" loses each loop whose absolute area is below `ISLAND_AREA_MIN` (1e-4 mm2).
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/slivers.rs`: new method `Region::without_slivers(min_area)`. It filters loops. It does not change a kept loop. A measure that is not positive and finite removes nothing.
- `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs`: one line, `mod slivers;`.

## Cause

The pocket family on a part cuts the enclosed area minus the part material that stands in it. The enclosed area and the part section share a wall. A clockwise loop of that kind stands outside each boundary. `Region::triangles` refuses the whole region with "hole outside any boundary". `selection_region` gives the same region to generation. Thus the slivers also reached generation. This fix removes them there too.

title: fix(xtask): the batch gate runs its suites in parallel lanes
body:
Stacked on #2779 (merge #2779 first)

Process change: yes

## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate batch` builds each crate alone first. There is one `debug build: <crate> (--no-run)` step for each crate.
- The batch tier then runs its suite steps in the parallel lanes that the release tier uses (`xtask/src/queue.rs`).
- A quick gate that falls back to the batch plan uses the lanes too.
- The batch queue takes its order from the newest `timings.tsv` of a `batch-*` or `release-*` run. The release queue reads `release-*` runs only, as before.
- The `heavy` tier of #2779 and a quick plan stay one step at a time.
- `AGENTS.md` (batch row of the tier table) and the `gate` skill describe the new batch tier.

The gate keeps its guarantees. Each step runs and has its own log. A red step fails the gate. A failed build stops the run. The checkout is read before each step (VOID). The builds, the `ISOLATED` targets, each ui step and clippy run alone with the whole job budget.

## Cause

- `Run::plan` used the lane queue only when the label was `release`. The batch tier ran each step after the other.
- `plan::batch` had one `--no-run` build for all the crates. `crates/kernel` has a dev-dependency on itself with the `truck` feature. The one build gave the shared dependencies the features of all the crates. A later step with one `-p <crate>` resolved a smaller feature set, and cargo compiled that crate again.

## Tests

Pins (all in `xtask`, red before the fix):

- `step_tests::batch_prebuilds_each_crate_without_mixing_feature_sets`
- `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep`
- `lanes_tests::batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings`
- `lanes_tests::batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release`

| `Run::new`: `lanes` on for `release` only | `batch_executor_overlaps_lanes_runs_isolated_alone_and_writes_timings` | red; green after the restore |
| `lanes::history_for`: `batch` reads `release-*` only | `batch_history_reads_newest_batch_or_falls_back_to_release` | red; green after the restore |

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green (1 step, `xtask unit tests`).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: no warnings.

## Wall time

One real `cargo xtask gate batch` run on head `1da2bcca2`: green, 929 steps, 0 failed.

| Reading | Value |

body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate light` is a new gate tier. It runs the light twins of the heavy tests in release.
- The plan is one release build of the crates that hold a twin. Then it has one step for each test target with a twin (`motion light: lib`).
- A light twin is found from the source. Its ignore reason starts with `light lane:`. Its name is `<full test>_light`.
- The planner refuses a twin by name when its file has no `#[ignore]`d full test. A twin cannot take the place of its full test.
- The first twin is `the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/tests.rs`. It plans the slot 2 times. The full sweep keeps its 20 rows and does not change.
- A red light run prints a note for the PR. The note names each red step and the command of its full heavy step: `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`.
- AGENTS.md has two new named rules: **The light lane** ("Testing") and **Local full rerun** ("Commits and Releases").
- `docs/decisions/2569-light-heavy-tier.md` records the choices.
- The branch was refreshed against `upstream/main` at `744c0847b`. The merge keeps the upstream `heavy` tier and the new `light` tier.
- The tier pins now check both parser variants, both help lines, both error lists, and both rules in AGENTS.md.

## Cause

- A heavy test was skipped for each patch or run in full at the cut. There was no tier between the two.
- A red heavy test stayed unseen until the cut gate. A red cut gate costs about 53 minutes.

## Tests

Pins, all in `xtask/src/light_tests.rs`:

- `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own`
- `light_plan_is_one_release_build_then_one_step_for_each_target_with_a_twin`
- `the_slot_sweep_keeps_its_full_test_and_has_a_light_twin`
- `a_light_twin_needs_its_name_and_its_full_test_next_to_it`
- `a_red_light_run_names_the_full_heavy_rerun_of_each_red_step`
- `the_law_names_the_light_lane_and_the_local_full_rerun`

Red before the change: yes. On unchanged code the pins do not compile (`unresolved import crate::light`). This is a new tier, thus there is no earlier behaviour to fail an assert.

Mutations:

- The refusal of a twin without its full test was removed: `a_light_twin_needs_its_name_and_its_full_test_next_to_it` was red. Restored: green.
- The `light` tier was removed from `parse_gate`: `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own` was red. Restored: green.
- The `light:` to `heavy:` mapping of the note was removed: `a_red_light_run_names_the_full_heavy_rerun_of_each_red_step` was red. Restored: green.
- A false assert was added to the twin: `cargo xtask gate light` was red (exit code 1) and printed the note with `cargo xtask gate release --only "motion heavy: lib"`. Restored: green.

Final-head mutations:

- Remove the `heavy` parser variant: `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own` fails with exit code 101. Restore it: green.
- Remove the `light` parser variant: `gate_light_is_a_tier_of_its_own` fails with exit code 101. Restore it: green.
- Remove the upstream heavy rule: `the_law_names_the_light_lane_and_the_local_full_rerun` fails with exit code 101. Restore it: green.
- All six `light_tests` pins pass after restoration.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green across the original run and the `--failed` rerun after local path recovery. All 9 selected steps pass.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: green: 2 of 2 steps pass. The release build took 1621 s. `motion light: lib` ran the slot twin: 1 passed, 0 failed, 26 s.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: exit 0: 217 steps, 0 gate failures, 134.9 min. Actual tests: 99 passed and 3 pre-existing known failures for #1950. The gate explicitly excludes those three red tests from its verdict.

- `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: green: clean in 3 min 55 s.

The first cached build stalled. The checks use `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET_DIR=target-verify CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1 RUSTC_WRAPPER=` in the same worktree. No source configuration changed.

The first quick run passed 8 of 9 steps:

title: fix(post): a flipped Z refusal names the exact reason
body:
## What changed

- A flipped WCS Z does not post. That does not change.
- The refusal now names the exact reason. The issue permits this result: "or the refusal names the exact reason and the decision is recorded".
- The post engine (`post::wcs_flip::apply`) and the verification gate (`app::setup_wcs_flip::setup_problem`) read the reason from one constant, `post::wcs_flip::Z_REASON`.
- The post engine adds a second clause only for a section that has a canned cycle.
- `docs/decisions/2474-wcs-flip-z-refusal.md` records the decision and answers the two open questions of the issue.

The new text of the post engine:

`operation Probe: the WCS has its Z axis flipped; posting a flipped Z is not supported yet - on a control that reads Z reversed, the tool-length word depends on how the tool lengths were measured (a preset length needs G44, a length touched off on that control needs G43), the project does not state which, and the wrong word moves the tool by twice its length; the section also has a canned cycle, whose R plane a mirrored Z puts on the far side of the hole bottom - clear Flip Z on the WCS page`

## Cause

- The old text gave a general reason: "tool-length compensation (G43) and the canned cycles' retract assume the controller's +Z leaves the work".
- The exact reason is this. The tool is on the physical "up" side of its tip. On a control that reads Z reversed, "up" is the control's -Z.
- A register with a preset length then needs G44. A register with a length touched off on that control needs G43.
- The project states only "Z is flipped". It does not state how the tool lengths were measured.
- The wrong word moves the tool by twice its length. The post cannot select the word, so it refuses.

## The maintainer decides

- This PR does not carry a flipped Z into the program. It closes the issue by the second "Done means" clause.
- A carry needs one new statement from the user: how the tool lengths of the flipped setup are measured. The decision file lists what that work includes.
- If the maintainer wants the carry, the issue stays open or a new issue has that work. This PR files no new issue.

## Tests

Pins:

- `a_flipped_z_refuses_by_name` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, extended).
- `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` (`crates/post/tests/wcs_flip.rs`, new).
- `a_flipped_z_refuses_the_post_by_name` (`crates/app/tests/wcs_flip_post.rs`, extended).

Red before the fix:

- The two post pins failed on unchanged code. The failure showed the old text.
- The app pin failed with the old `setup_wcs_flip.rs`. The failure showed the old text.

Mutations:

- Old `crates/post/src/post/wcs_flip.rs`: the two post pins are red. Restored: green.
- Old `crates/app/src/setup_wcs_flip.rs`: the app pin is red. Restored: green.
- The cycle clause printed for each section (`if true`): `a_flipped_z_without_a_cycle_names_the_tool_length_word_only` is red. Restored: green.

Gate:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 8 steps, 0 failed (post lib, `wcs_flip`, `wcs_flip_dialects`, app lib, app `wcs_flip`, app `wcs_flip_post`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- The gate ran with `CAMCRAFT_NO_SCCACHE=1` and an empty `RUSTC_WRAPPER`. The sccache server of the build machine did not answer, and each build stopped after some crates.

Heavy gate evidence from the latest review:

- Command: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`.
- Tested PR head: `21c04620607e3d66e5ee738c2dffc65445978c1e`.
- Result: PASS, 184 steps, 0 failed, 21.6 minutes. The registered #1950 test failed at its expected assertion. The gate confirmed this expected failure.
- The reviewer ran the heavy gate locally after a trial merge with main `744c0847b04d54cfc6e3e8b24a21520c40b6bcef`.
- The final trial merge used main `f3b0e195503466db86b0ff0b15dbf614153e1bb4`. The app and dependency sources were unchanged between the two tested trees.
- [All reached heavy lanes and their results](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/2785#issuecomment-7018788718) appear in the latest review's detailed table. The table names each reached target and gives its pass count. A zero count means no ignored test ran in that target.

None. No `.nc` or `.cl` file changes. No posted program changes: the change is in refusal text only.

## Not exercised

- The machine door (`machine::untranslated_inversion`, an inverted machine Z) keeps its old text. It is not in the scope of this issue.

## Overlaps

Effort: max

title: feat(ui): stock axis choice on the Stock page (along Z, X, Y or custom)
body:
## What changed

- The Stock page has a "Stock axis" choice: Along Z (default), Along X, Along Y and Custom. Custom shows three angles in degrees: turn about Z (yaw), tilt about Y (pitch), tilt about X (roll). The choice applies to a box and to a cylinder. The old "Rotation (yaw deg)" row is replaced.
- The turn is stored in the stock's existing `Location.rot`. There is no new shape field and no project-file version step.
- Apply sends the whole turn through the undoable `SetStock` (new UI queue entry `CommandKind::SetStockPose`; the old `CommandKind::SetStock { yaw_deg }` stays for its callers). Undo restores the old turn.
- The page reads a stored turn back. A preset turn shows its preset. Any other turn shows Custom with its angles (`camcraft_geometry::geometry::stock_axis`).
- Before any simulation, the page shows a plain note when the simulation cannot cut the drafted stock: a cylinder laid along X or Y, or a stock tilted off the axes. The note asks the simulation's own law (`stock_follow::sim_frame`). The refusals `OBLIQUE_STOCK` and `LAID_CYLINDER` do not change. A box laid along X or Y is a square turn, so the simulation cuts it and no note shows.
- MCP `set_stock` takes an optional `axis` ("z", "x", "y") or `angles_deg` ({yaw, pitch, roll}), not both. It calls the same `SetStock` and returns `{ stock, axis, angles_deg }`. The camcraft-mcp skill row is updated.
- `sketch.rs`: the DXF profile face ignored the stock's turn. Now an upright stock keeps its top face, a stock laid square is read as the same solid unturned, and a laid cylinder or a tilted stock is refused by name (`sketch::NO_TOP_FACE`). `ImportDxf` shows that refusal.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/2576-stock-axis.md`.
- Follow-up: #2758 (stock simulation: cut a cylinder or box stock that lies along X or Y).

Process change: yes

## Readings

- X preset = a quarter turn about Y (stock Z goes to world +X). Y preset = a minus quarter turn about X (stock Z goes to world +Y).

title: feat(sim): step the simulation to the next or the previous operation
body: ## What changed The simulation transport bar has two new buttons, **Previous op** and **Next op**, between Stop and the slider. Page Up and Page Down do the same steps. - **Next op** moves the playhead to the start of the next operation in program order, and pauses the playback. - **Previous op** moves to the start of the current operation. A second press moves to the start of the one before it. - The readout already names the current operation (`Contour1 · RAPID · ...`). After a step it names the new operation. - **Next** is disabled in the last operation. **Previous** is disabled at the start of the first operation. Both are disabled while the stock removal is calculated, as the slider is (#2611). - The tips (and the AccessKit descriptions) say what each step does, name the target operation and name the key. - A step across a setup boundary, a tool change or a WCS change is the same step. An operation with no toolpath is not on the timeline, so it is no stop. - The user guide (`guide/operations` "Checking") describes the two steps. The lookup is on `sim::Script` in `camcraft-sim` (`crates/sim/src/sim_steps.rs`: `op_starts`, `next_op_start`, `prev_op_start`, `op_starting_at`), so the stand-alone simulator (#2587) can use the same steps. The UI part is `crates/ui/src/egui_app/sim_steps.rs`; `shell.rs` gets one call. An operation starts at its first segment on the timeline (the connector rapid, when there is one). At that position all moves of the earlier operations are complete. A step is a scrub to that time, so the stock follows the playhead as for a scrub. Decision record: `docs/decisions/2608-sim-op-step.md`. ## Screenshots Headless render at 2x, dark theme, two operations, playhead at 1.0 s. title: feat(2d): Slot Undercut for T-slot, keyseat, dovetail and lollipop cutters
body:
## What changed

This PR adds the Slot Undercut operation and the cutters for it.

- **Four cutter kinds** in `camcraft-tools`: `t_slot`, `keyseat`, `dovetail`, `lollipop`. They use the existing tool fields. `diameter` is the head. `flute_len` is the head height. `shank_d` and `shank_len` are the neck. `tip_angle` is the dovetail flank angle. The kind words are additive, so `PROJECT_VERSION` does not change. The starter catalog has one cutter of each kind.
- **One generator** in `camcraft-motion` (`machining2d::undercut`). It cuts a straight slot or a circular slot (DXF-style bulge). It changes Z at one XY station only, outside the wall. It feeds in sideways, cuts the centre pass and the radial stepover passes at one depth, feeds out the same way, then lifts. The pass offset comes from the widest point of the cutter profile, not from the tip.
- **One verify law** in `camcraft-sim` (`Mode::Undercut`, `verify/undercut.rs`). A move that changes Z while material is in or over the head is `Warning::UndercutLift`. It blocks the post. A neck or holder band with material above its bottom is a `ShankHit`. The operation layer reads the two again against the stock that the earlier operations left (`acquit_undercut_by_prior`). A neck slot that an earlier Slot operation cut is then air.
- **The true profile in the solid law.** The solid law judges a dovetail as a frustum and a lollipop as a full ball (`Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`). The head top gets the same allowance as the tip, so a head that stands under its roof is contact and not a gouge.
- **The true profile in the field stock simulation** (`Stock::simulate_undercut`, `Stock::with_partial_undercut`, `SdfTool::Dovetail`). The head and the neck are two convex solids. The field keeps their union. Both the stock view and Simulate playback cut the head and neck with it. Notice `cut_twin_work::twin_tool` maps `SdfTool::Dovetail` to `"dovetail"`.
- **The column engines cut nothing for an undercut.** A column has one top for each (x, y). It cannot hold air below material.
- **App**: `OpParams::SlotUndercut` (kind tag 44, appended), the project file mirror (keeping `0.0` `bulge` and `neck_slot` keys in JSON), the stamp digest, heights, the part solid law for a part source, and the kept-parts law for both stock and part sources.
- **MCP**: `add_operation` with kind `Slot Undercut` (key `slot_undercut`) and `add_tool` with the new kind words. `verify` reports the new finding kind `undercut_lift`. `list_operation_types` and `edit_operation` include `bulge` and `neck_slot` when they equal `0.0`.
- **UI**: the four undercut kinds in the tool editor (`tool_undercut_row.rs` seeds valid defaults, `Flank angle (deg)` / `flank angle °` edits `ToolKind::Dovetail`, and `Corner radius` stays hidden for undercut kinds), the Slot Undercut page (`undercut_page.rs`), and five original icons (SVG masters rendered with `cargo xtask icons`).
- **Docs**: a Slot Undercut section in the 2D operations guide, and `docs/decisions/1444-slot-undercut.md`.

## UI screenshots

Before/after renders from the headless `ShellUi` (`1440x960` WGPU) on `upstream/main` (`5ed5b7fe2`) and this PR branch (images stored on `mkinney/Camcraft` `pr-screenshots` commit `0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86`):

| View | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tool editor (`DT-20-60` dovetail cutter) | ![Tool editor before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-before.png) | ![Tool editor after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/tool-editor-after.png) |
| Slot Undercut page (`TSlot` in milling setup) | ![Slot Undercut before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-before.png) | ![Slot Undercut after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/0fd64401cc4acd068a1ec9e048417002176a3f86/2714/slot-undercut-after.png) |

## Cause

There was no cutter kind with a head wider than its neck, and no operation for one. The laws for a plain contour are wrong below a roof. The column model reads a pass as a cleared kerf, so a lift through the roof passes as a retract in its own kerf.

## Tests

New pins cover the new behaviour. Each review fix below also has a direct test and mutation check.

- `camcraft-tools --lib` (`107 passed; 0 failed`): `undercut::tests` checks sane cutters, refusals by name, the profile contact point, and the drawn outline.
- `camcraft-motion --lib` (`459 passed; 0 failed; 10 ignored`): `machining2d::undercut::tests` pins single-station Z moves, entry slot refusals, concentric arc slots, profile contact offsets, and input refusals.
- `camcraft-sim --test undercut_laws` (`14 passed; 0 failed`): pins `UndercutLift`, `ShankHit`, `acquit_undercut_by_prior`, `Prof::Dove`, `Prof::Ball`, `Atom::cap`, and `Stock::simulate_undercut`.
- `camcraft-app --test mcp_slot_undercut` (`7 passed; 0 failed`): pins MCP cutting, verification, posting, refusals, `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts`, and `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play` (`8 passed; 0 failed`): pins `playback_removes_undercut_head_and_neck_and_matches_field_view`.
- `camcraft-app --test stock_play_partial` (`4 passed; 0 failed`): pins `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy`.
- `camcraft-motion --test golden_undercut`: pins four golden CL files. The generator suite and its unchanged goldens now live in `crates/motion/tests/`.
- `camcraft-app --test tool_law` (`5 passed; 0 failed`): pins undercut cutter compatibility.
- `camcraft-ui --lib` (`1256 passed; 0 failed; 7 ignored`): includes `tool_undercut_row::tests`, `tool_cutter_params::each_milling_kind_shows_the_parameters_its_outline_is_drawn_from`, and `tests/tool_undercut.rs` (`new_tool_undercut_kinds_seed_sane_defaults_hide_corner_radius_and_show_dovetail_flank_angle`, `dovetail_properties_and_editor_edit_flank_angle_without_corner_radius`, and `slot_undercut_page_shows_its_geometry_heights_passes_and_feeds_fields`).

Review-fix mutation checks (guard reverted -> RED, restored -> GREEN):

- UI dovetail flank angle, undercut defaults, and corner-radius filter reverted: RED (`3 failed` across `tests/tool_undercut.rs` and `tool_cutter_params`). Restored: GREEN (`11 passed; 0 failed`).
- `is_part_kept_kind` reverted in `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs`: `a_part_source_undercut_keeps_neighbouring_parts` RED (`post` succeeded instead of refusing). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).
- `skip_serializing_if = "is_zero"` restored in `crates/app/src/project/undercut_dto.rs`: `list_operation_types_and_edit_operation_keep_zero_bulge_and_neck_slot` RED (`list_operation_types` omitted `bulge` and `neck_slot`). Restored: GREEN (`7 passed; 0 failed`).

Restoring `stock_play.rs` alone kept `partial_move_cuts_undercut_head_and_neck_on_a_copy` RED. Restored both: GREEN (`8 passed; 0 failed` and `4 passed; 0 failed`).

Gate on `b95c27b2e52fc8b976ce9372bcc5e4141c247113`: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 651 steps with zero failures (45.9 minutes). The merged main revision is `e5b0ca3c1`. It includes #2767, which fixes the four reviewed area-preview failures. The UI unit suite passed 1,258 tests (7 ignored). All 16 UI integration suites passed. `cargo clippy -j 12 -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with zero warnings.

Latest review-fix checks:

- The motion `golden_undercut` suite passed all four tests. Removing the motion test target gave RED. A feed change from 120 to 121 made all four goldens fail. Restoring the suite and feed returned all four tests to GREEN. The four CL files moved without byte changes.
- Reverting the main geometry fix gave exactly the four reviewed frame-cost failures. Restoring it returned all eight frame-cost tests to GREEN.

Current merge blocker: main advanced to `744c0847b04d54cfc6e3e8b24a21520c40b6bcef` during validation. A later local refresh exposes safety overlaps: `verify/avoid_poly.rs:25` omits `Atom::cap`, and `verify/swept.rs:130` omits `Prof::Dove` and `Prof::Ball` in keep-out dilation. The refresh compile checks and clippy are RED. The gate was stopped after the compile failures. No new collision semantics were selected. Local commit `b8c5cb42e` is not pushed. The pushed head and its GREEN gate remain `b95c27b2e`. The `Addressed:` comment records the blocker.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden changed. Four golden CL files are new:

- `slot_undercut_tslot_straight.cl`
- `slot_undercut_keyseat_arc.cl`
- `slot_undercut_dovetail_straight.cl`
